title: Collision Avoidance Arena
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A top-down p5.js simulation of a robot running the Chapter 10 collision avoidance program in a walled arena with three boxes. Students tune STOP_DIST_CM, SLOW_DIST_CM, full speed, and the turn strategy, then observe the path, motor duty, turn count, floor coverage, and wall touches.

learningObjectives: Adjust STOP_DIST_CM and SLOW_DIST_CM and predict how the robot's path, speed, and number of turns will change
Explain how the three zones (FORWARD, SLOW, TURN) map to go_forward(), go_slow(), and the stop-and-turn branch
Explain why a small stop distance at high speed causes wall touches, using loop delay and stopping distance
Compare random turns with always-left turns in terms of floor coverage and repeated paths

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Return the robot to the center and clear counters, keeping slider settings

controls.label: Clear Path
controls.purpose: Erase the path trace and covered-floor squares

controls.label: Slow distance (cm)
controls.purpose: SLOW_DIST_CM, kept at least 5 cm above the stop distance

controls.label: Drop robot
controls.purpose: Place the robot on the floor with a random heading

equations: turn = 0.4 s spin of about 90 degrees
assumptions: The ToF sensor reports the nearest object in a 10 degree cone with about 1 cm of noise
Wheel speed changes with a short lag (0.08 s time constant) instead of instantly
Arena is 360 x 240 cm with three fixed boxes
limitations: No wheel slip, battery sag, or motor mismatch
The sensor never misreads dark or shiny surfaces

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with a running simulation and live readouts
keyQuestions: What happens to the number of turns when you raise STOP_DIST_CM?
Why does the robot touch walls when the stop distance is 5 cm at 100 cm/s?
Why does Always left stop finding new floor after a while?
Which threshold pair would you copy into config.py for your classroom floor, and why?
commonMisconceptions: The robot stops exactly at the stop distance (it keeps rolling during the loop delay and while the wheels slow down)
A smaller stop distance is always better because the robot gets closer to things
The sensor sees everything in front of the robot (it only sees a narrow cone straight ahead)
assessmentOpportunities: Data table of turns, coverage, and wall touches for three stop distances
Exit ticket explaining two fixes for a robot that bumps into boxes
Written comparison of random and always-left turn strategies
